We also present many open questions that we view as natural “next step” questions, given our current state of knowledge. 1.1 Basic Definitions Before any further discussion, we give the basic definitions related to arithmetic circuits. Definition 1.1 (Arithmetic circuits). An arithmetic circuit Φ over the field F and the set of variables X (usually, X = {x1 , . . . , xn }) is a directed acyclic graph as follows. The vertices of Φ are called gates. Every gate in Φ of in-degree 0 is labeled by either a variable from X or a field element from F. Every other gate in Φ is labeled by either × or + and has in-degree 2. An arithmetic circuit is called a formula if it is a direct

Intuitively, such circuits compute polynomials in a “straightforward” way, as there are no cancelations during the computation. This simple model of computation has been studied in many works, and exponential lower bounds for the size of monotone circuits are well known (this is true for the arithmetic case as well as for the Boolean case).
